key_insight: Lotus AI enrollees had substantial chronic disease burden and fragmented care, highlighting care coordination as a core design requirement for physician-supervised AI platforms.
clinical_relevance: The enrollee profile suggests these platforms need workflows for chronic conditions and functional or symptom-defined disorders, not just episodic care.
method: Characterized 3,223 enrollees who completed onboarding, messaged the agent, and had linked health records during February–July 2026.
Compared enrollee demographics and chronic condition prevalence with national benchmarks.
Examined care fragmentation and physician escalations, laboratory orders, and prescriptions by disorder status.
evidence_signal: Chronic condition prevalence exceeded age-specific national estimates by 4–7 percentage points; users with functional disorders had 1.8× as many physician escalations and 2.6× as many laboratory orders, but no more prescriptions.
watch_item: This selected, single-platform observational cohort does not establish clinical benefit or generalizability to other AI care populations.
paper_title: Enrollees and Early Lessons from an Agentic Healthcare Platform with Physicians in the Loop
